reader.title: Shooting of Jeb Barganier
bases: A sheriff's deputy shot a Black man who fled as the sheriff's force tried to serve a warrant at his home; no crowd or mob is mentioned (A1).
One short item in the Montgomery Advertiser is the only report; no second white or any Black-press account was found (A1).

summary.text: The shooting of Jeb Barganier took place on the night of August 5, 1920, when a sheriff's deputy shot Barganier, a Black man, as deputies tried to serve a warrant at his home.
The bullet passed through his elbow and broke the bone.
The Montgomery Advertiser reported the shooting the next day as a case of a man shot "while resisting arrest"; no other account of it was found.
The "Sheriff's force" went to Barganier's home to serve a warrant, the nature of which the report does not give.
The item carries no dateline, but it ran among local news on the Advertiser's second page, which suggests the Montgomery area.
While deputies were trying to get in at the front door, Barganier "made a break from the back door taking the door bar with him."
Deputy Tucker met him at the back door, and on seeing Tucker, Barganier ran.
Deputy sheriff Ellington then shot him through the elbow, breaking the bone.
The coverage does not say what charge the warrant carried, whether Barganier was taken into custody, or whether the shooting was investigated.

The Montgomery Advertiser ran the story as a three-paragraph item headed "Negro Shot While Resisting Arrest," giving the officers' version as fact and calling Barganier "the negro" throughout while referring to the deputy as "Mr. Tucke."

Although the headline and opening sentence describe resistance, the account itself describes only flight: Barganier ran out the back carrying the door bar and "made a break to get awav [away]" before he was shot.
No other white paper and no Black newspaper is known to have reported the shooting.

accounts.label: Officers' account as printed by the Montgomery Advertiser
accounts.gist: Deputies came to serve a warrant; while they tried to enter at the front, Barganier broke out the back door carrying the door bar, ran on seeing deputy Tucker, and was shot by deputy Ellington.

framing.detail: The headline 'Negro Shot While Resisting Arrest' and the phrase 'while resisting arrest' present the shooting as justified, though the account itself describes Barganier running away.
